title: docs: self-hosting's env-var row flags Turso's driver as an optional package but not Postgres's or MySQL's, which are optional the same way
body:
Split out of #14510 by triage. #14510 found that a plain CLI install has no `pg`, so the documented Postgres self-host path fails at boot; its remedies split into a **packaging** decision (bake drivers into the runtime image / have the scaffolder add them) and a **docs** correction. The packaging half is a maintainer call and stays on #14510. This card is the docs half, which is owed under every one of those directions and should not wait behind the decision.

## Measured at `origin/main` `4a37870`

`packages/drivers/driver-sql/package.json`:

```json
"peerDependencies":     { "mysql2": "^3.0.0", "pg": "^8.0.0", "tedious": "^18.0.0" },
"peerDependenciesMeta": { "mysql2": {"optional":true}, "pg": {"optional":true}, "tedious": {"optional":true} },
"optionalDependencies": { "better-sqlite3": "^13.0.3" }
```

`pg`, `mysql2` and `tedious` are optional peers — npm 7+ auto-installs peer deps but skips optional ones, so a plain install has none of them. `better-sqlite3` is a real optional dependency and does get installed.

`content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx:35` — the `OS_DATABASE_URL` row — offers five URL spellings and is already careful about this exact class of problem for one of them:

> `libsql://` / Turso is inferred, but its driver is an **optional** package — `npm install @objectstack/driver-turso`, or the boot fails loudly rather than degrading to SQLite

It then gives MySQL three dialect caveats and MongoDB a single-tenancy caveat. **Neither `postgres://…` nor `mysql://…` carries the optional-package note**, even though both need one installed exactly as Turso does. The same page advertises `postgres://` invocations at `:74`, `:93`, `:153` and `:202`.

So the page already knows the shape of this warning, gives it to the one driver that ships as an ObjectStack package, and omits it for the two that ship as third-party ones.

## Fix

Give `postgres://…` and `mysql://…` the same optional-package note the Turso spelling has, naming the package to install (`pg`, `mysql2`) and saying the boot fails loudly without it. Same row, same wording pattern. Check the bare-Node recipe on the same page (`npm install -g @objectstack/cli` followed by a Postgres `EnvironmentFile`) and give it the install step too.

Worth checking whether `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers` — which that row links to — has the same gap; this card measured only `self-hosting.mdx`.

## Why this is owed regardless of how #14510 is decided

Even if the runtime image bakes `pg` in and the scaffolder adds it, the bare-Node reader who installs the CLI globally still needs the note — that is the audience #14510 itself separates out ("1 and 3 address different audiences"). If the packaging decision goes the other way, the note is the whole fix. There is no direction under which this text is wrong to add.

⛔ Do not use this card to change any packaging: no dependency moves, no Dockerfile edits, no scaffolder changes. Those are #14510's, and pre-empting them here would decide the question this split exists to leave open.

Refs: #14510 (the parent finding and the packaging decision).
